source_text: Quasi iacenti in corporeis dicit: Exsurge; oboedienti: proxima mea, columba mea. Ne trepidet ad turbines, adnuntiat hiemem discessisse et pluviam abiisse sibi — vitia sibi abeunt, nullam apud Deum mansionem habentia.
pass_a_gloss: As-if to-one-lying in bodily-things he-says: Rise-up; to-obeying-one: near-one my, dove my. Lest she-may-tremble at whirlwinds, he-announces winter to-have-departed and rain to-have-gone to-itself — vices to-themselves depart, no with God dwelling having.
pass_b_english: As to one still lying among bodily things he says: [[Arise >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:10]]; to the one who obeys: my near one, my dove. Lest she tremble at whirlwinds, he announces that winter has departed and the rain gone off to itself — vices depart to themselves, having no dwelling with God.
